messages:
Linda (CS): Hey team — escalation from AcmeCorp. They saw a sudden run of 429s yesterday evening during a marketing blast. They say traffic spiked ~6x for ~90s and their app hit errors despite being on a paid plan. Can we confirm if they exhausted burst credits or hit a per-minute quota?

Maria (Support): On it. I pulled their usage window — looks like a short ramp starting at 18:12 UTC, peaked for ~75s, then dropped. Request graph shows a sharp step. BillingBot shows no billing anomalies, but I see a drop in x-rate-limit-remaining in logs.

Josh (SRE): Quick checklist: 1) check rate-limit response headers in the failed requests 2) check internal burst-credits telemetry (we emit burst_credit_balance per-customer) 3) confirm if any fallback routing happened. Can you share sample headers / request IDs?

Linda (CS): Pasted one failed response from their app: 

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1678902782
X-Burst-Credits: 0
Retry-After: 30
{ "error": "rate_exceeded" }

Maria (Support): That X-Burst-Credits: 0 is telling. Looks like they used up the short-term bank. Do we know their plan's baseline burst size?

Devon - ProdEng: AcmeCorp is on Growth monthly. Policy: tokens minted at 10 credits/sec (configurable per plan) with a max burst bank of 600 credits. That should handle ~60 concurrent single-token requests for ~10s. If they saw a 6x sustained spike for 75s, bank would deplete.

Josh (SRE): Two modes of mitigation: client-side and server-side. Client-side: exponential backoff + jitter, and detect Retry-After. Server-side options we can consider immediately: short-term increase of burst bank for this tenant (manual emergency ops), or enable smoothing (leaky bucket) to spread excess into a small queue for up to N seconds.

Maria (Support): Customer asked for recommended retry/backoff behaviour. Suggested reply: respect Retry-After if present, otherwise do exponential backoff starting at 200ms with full jitter, cap at 10s. Avoid tight loops. Also recommend token-batching on their side if they're fan-out heavy.

Linda (CS): They also asked why the 429s happened quickly instead of graceful throttling. Is our smoothing policy aggressive?

Devon - ProdEng: Our default aggressive policy prefers fail-fast to protect other tenants. Smoothing (gradual accept queue) is opt-in at account-level because it increases tail latency and can impact throughput. We do offer a per-customer smoothing window parameter (smoothing_window_ms) which shapes peak ingress into a leak rate. Default smoothing_window_ms is 0 (disabled) for Growth; Enterprise can enable 2s-10s windows.

Josh (SRE): For this support run, options: 1) short-term increase to burst bank (we can add +1200 credits for 10 minutes) 2) enable smoothing window = 3000ms for the tenant for 30 minutes to absorb spikes 3) advise client to implement retries. I'd vote for combining 1+3 as fastest.

Maria (Support): Customer prefers minimal code changes — they'd rather we do server-side smoothing temporarily. Can we toggle that?

DeployBot: deploy scheduled: enable_smoothing(account_id=acmecorp, window_ms=3000) by jenkins-deploy at 18:55 UTC — pending approval.

Josh (SRE): I'll approve emergency toggle. Devon, are there any risks to enable smoothing for a single tenant?

Devon - ProdEng: Low risk; we limit per-tenant smoothing to a max in-flight queue depth (1000 requests) and we isolate queues per-region. Edge cases: if they retry aggressively while smoothing is active we could increase processing load; recommend we temporarily set their concurrent_workers cap to +20% and enable burst-credit topup. Also enable request tracing for their request IDs.

Josh (SRE): I'll provision +20% workers for their pool and top up 1200 credits for 15 minutes. I'll also add a transient alert: if CPU or queue depth > 70% OR error rate > 1% we'll rollback.

Maria (Support): Patch message ready to send to customer: "We observed your spike depleted the short-term burst bank. We've temporarily increased your burst credits and enabled a 3s smoothing window to absorb traffic bursts. Please implement retries with exponential backoff (200ms base) to avoid tight retry storms. Monitoring is in place; we'll revert changes in 30 minutes unless you request otherwise." Thoughts?

Linda (CS): Sounds good. Also ask them for SDK request IDs for a full audit.

BillingBot: Note: manual burst-credit top-up applied to acmecorp at 18:57 UTC (+1200 credits, expires 19:12 UTC). No billing charge for emergency top-up; internal cost center: ENG-OPS.

Josh (SRE): After toggles went live we saw a smoothing queue in region-us-east activate and the client's 429 rate dropped from ~12% to ~0.8% within ~45s. Queue depth peaked at 420 and drained. CPU increased but under the 70% threshold. Good result.

Devon - ProdEng: Follow-ups we should do: 1) offer them a permanent smoothing option for their plan with defined SLO tradeoffs 2) recommend a capacity reservation for campaign windows (reserved capacity or scheduled burst window) 3) provide sample SDK snippet for recommended backoff. Example snippet: 

```js
// simple retry with exponential backoff + jitter
async function callWithRetry(fn, attempts = 6) {
  for (let i = 0; i < attempts; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (err) {
      if (err.status !== 429) throw err;
      const base = 200 * Math.pow(2, i);
      const jitter = Math.random() * 100;
      const wait = Math.min(10000, base + jitter);
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, wait));
    }
  }
  throw new Error('max-retries-exceeded');
}
```

Maria (Support): Also pulled their token-bucket metrics. Attached summary: minted_rate = 10 credits/s, bank_max = 600, observed_peak_rate ~ 58 credits/s for 75s. That math explains exhaustion.

Linda (CS): Customer acceptance: they replied "Thanks — saw immediate improvement, will add retry code and check with us about permanent smoothing or reserved capacity."

Josh (SRE): Action items: 
- [ ] Devon: draft permanent smoothing SKU and SLO tradeoffs (due EOD)
- [ ] Billing: propose add-on pricing for scheduled burst windows
- [ ] Support: send SDK snippet + recommended retry guidance to customer (Maria)
- [ ] SRE: keep transient telemetry for 24h and close incident if stable (Josh)

Maria (Support): Done — sending final note now. Will include request IDs and encourage them to reach back if they see retries/duplicates.

Linda (CS): Closing loop with customer. Good cross-team response.

Josh (SRE): Postmortem note: root cause = short-duration high fan-out that exceeded minted token rate and depleted burst bank; remediation = transient top-up + smoothing + client retries; long-term = offer scheduled capacity or permanent smoothing add-on. Logging this to incidents channel.

DeployBot: change complete: smoothing enabled for acmecorp in us-east at 18:59 UTC.

Maria (Support): Marking thread resolved for now. If queue or 429s reappear we'll reopen. :thumbsup:

Linda (CS): Thanks all.
